rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with the provided Gardner 3AB data, but it overstates quality by calling the embryo good-to-excellent and inaccurately paraphrases TE B as 'few cells, loose epithelium,' which is closer to a poorer TE description. No image was available, so no true image-based morphology was possible.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor diagnosis, endometrial thickness, sperm quality, BMI, prior cycle history, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and generally logical, with probability estimates tied to favorable and unfavorable factors. Minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments and overconfident statements about specific factor effects.

Largely aligned with IVF practice, especially recommending single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst. Small deviations include suggesting assisted hatching and ERA/PGT-A somewhat more readily than guideline-based routine practice would support.

Provides clear practical recommendations for transfer strategy, luteal support, transfer technique review, and contingency planning. Some suggestions are useful but a few are somewhat generic or not strongly evidence-based for this exact scenario.
